content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provides a comprehensive range of resources and updates to help individuals, healthcare professionals, and emergency responders prepare for and respond to public health emergencies. Below are detailed descriptions of the information and guidance available: 1. EPIC Webinar on August 16: This webinar focuses on strategies for effectively communicating public health emergency messages to diverse populations, using insights from California and Los Angeles County's experiences. 2. COCA Call on July 16: This session provides an update on the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A (H5N1) virus, offering critical information for clinicians and healthcare centers to manage and respond to this threat. 3. Hurricane Preparedness: Guidance is available on how to protect yourself and your loved ones before, during, and after a hurricane. This includes evacuation planning, securing your home, and staying safe during the storm. 4. Flood Safety: Learn how to prepare for floods, remain safe during flooding events, and protect your health when returning home after a flood. This includes creating emergency kits, understanding evacuation routes, and addressing potential health hazards like mold. 5. COCA Calls and Updates: June 27: Clinical management and outbreak updates on Mpox. February 29: Discussion on overdoses involving xylazine mixed with fentanyl, including clinical and public health implications. February 1: Diagnostic testing and treatment guidelines for COVID-19 and influenza. 6. Protecting Yourself and Your Loved Ones: Resources are available to help individuals understand various types of emergencies and the steps necessary to stay safe during these events. 7. Emergency Health Professional Resources: First responders, clinicians, and laboratorians can access specialized tools and training to enhance their emergency response capabilities. 8. CDC Agency-Wide Responses: Updates on current and recent public health emergencies, including responses to COVID-19, lung injuries, and Ebola outbreaks. 9. Communication Programs: COCA (Clinician Outreach and Communication Activity): Webinars, newsletters, and other resources to keep clinicians informed about public health emergencies. HAN (Health Alert Network): Alerts and guidance on urgent public health issues for professionals and clinicians. EPIC (Emergency Partners Information Connection): Information exchange to promote safety and health during emergencies. CERC (Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication): Training and tools for effective communication during crises. 10. Featured Calls and Webinars: October 26: Protecting infants from Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). September 21: Diagnostic algorithms for endemic mycoses, including blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis, and histoplasmosis. 11. Public Health Matters Blog: Practical skills to learn before an emergency. Tips for preparing your health to evacuate. Building trauma-informed communities. Emergency preparedness tips for parents of children with special healthcare needs. Must-haves for a first-aid kit. 12. Seasonal and Specific Emergency Preparedness: Winter Weather: Learn how to prepare for winter storms, prevent cold-related health issues, and stay safe during extreme weather. Extreme Heat: Recognize symptoms of heat-related illnesses and understand how to prevent and treat them. Earthquakes: Guidance on actions to take before, during, and after an earthquake to ensure safety. Tornado Recovery: Safety precautions to avoid injury after a tornado. 13. Mental Health During Disasters: Resources are available to help individuals manage emotional health during emergencies, enabling clear thinking and effective responses to urgent needs. 14. Health Alert Network (HAN): HAN 428: Update and interim guidance on the COVID-19 outbreak as of February 28, 2020. HAN 427: Interim guidance on the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) outbreak. 15. Prepare Your Health: Comprehensive resources to help individuals and families prepare for a wide range of emergencies, including reviewing important paperwork and creating emergency plans. 16. Psychological First Aid: Training and resources to address mental health distress during disasters, ensuring individuals and communities can recover effectively. 17. Staying Connected: The CDC encourages individuals to stay informed by subscribing to health alerts, webinars, and safety tips through email or social media platforms. These resources are designed to equip individuals, healthcare professionals, and emergency responders with the knowledge and tools necessary to navigate public health emergencies effectively.
